complete.problem: A force of 20 N pushes a box 5 m along the floor. Calculate the work done.

steps.text: Recall the equation: work done = force x distance moved in the direction of the force.
steps.annotation: Work is the energy transferred when a force moves an object.

steps.text: Substitute the values: work done = 20 N x 5 m.
steps.annotation: The distance must be measured along the line of action of the force.
Force in newtons times distance in metres gives energy in joules.

complete.selfExplanation: Explain why no work is done on the box if it does not move, even when the force is large.

faded.problem: A machine transfers 600 J of energy in 30 s. Calculate its power.

steps.text: Recall the equation: power = energy transferred / time taken.
steps.annotation: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred.

steps.text: Substitute the values: power = 600 J / 30 s.
steps.annotation: Time must be in seconds so the power comes out in watts.
One watt is one joule transferred per second.

faded.selfExplanation: The first step is shown. State the substitution you would make and the unit of the answer.

paired.problem: Calculate the kinetic energy of a 2 kg ball moving at 3 m/s.
paired.solution: Kinetic energy = 1/2 x m x v^2 = 1/2 x 2 kg x (3 m/s)^2 = 1/2 x 2 x 9 = 9 J. The speed is squared before multiplying by the mass.
